title: Luxury Guests Keep One Hotel Group Strong

source.author: Montira Rungjirajittranon
source.title: Thai Luxury Leads Minor’s Quarter Despite Tourist Slump
source.note: Single source. Thailand arrivals 'down 4.1%' left out: the source does not state the comparison period. Currency given only as the source's US dollar conversion.

figures.text: Minor core profit +13% year over year in Q3, to THB 2.1 billion (about $62.9 million)
figures.quote: Minor’s core profit rose 13% year over year to THB 2.1 billion (about $62.9 million)

figures.text: Anantara hotels in Thailand: RevPAR +19% like-for-like in Q3, average daily rate +13%
figures.quote: Minor’s Anantara-branded high-end hotels in Thailand reported a 19% like-for-like increase in RevPAR in the third quarter, on a 13% rise in average daily rate

figures.text: all Thai hotels RevPAR +13%, strongest of any major market in the group
figures.quote: Across all of Minor’s Thai hotels, RevPAR rose 13%, the strongest growth of any major market in the group

figures.text: Thailand cut 2026 international arrivals forecast to 33 million from 36.7 million
figures.quote: Thailand cutting its 2026 international arrivals forecast to 33 million from 36.7 million

figures.text: Cushman & Wakefield: luxury holding up better because guests less price sensitive
figures.quote: Cushman & Wakefield told Skift luxury was holding up better than the rest of the market because guests in that segment are less price sensitive.

figures.text: finished $50 million renovation of Anantara Siam Bangkok in September, all 335 rooms
figures.quote: It finished a $50 million renovation of Anantara Siam Bangkok in September, refurbishing all 335 rooms

figures.text: Maldives: Minor operates nine resorts, RevPAR +10%
figures.quote: The Maldives, where Minor operates nine resorts, also improved: RevPAR rose 10%

figures.text: Middle East & Africa RevPAR -11% in Q3; reason: regional conflict, weaker travel demand
figures.quote: RevPAR across Minor’s Middle East & Africa hotels fell 11% in the third quarter ... Minor cited the regional conflict and associated weaker travel demand.

figures.text: Middle East & Africa RevPAR -15% over nine months
figures.quote: Over nine months, the region’s RevPAR is down 15%.

figures.text: Marriott Middle East RevPAR -12% in Q3
figures.quote: Marriott’s Middle East RevPAR fell 12% in the third quarter

figures.text: Marriott mostly earns fees in Middle East; region about 3% of its global fees
figures.quote: Marriott mostly earns fees in the Middle East, and the region accounts for only about 3% of its global fees.

figures.text: Minor owns about 40% of its Middle East & Africa hotels
figures.quote: Minor, for its part, owns about 40% of its Middle East & Africa hotels

figures.text: almost 70% of Minor's whole portfolio owned or leased
figures.quote: Minor’s portfolio as a whole, where almost 70% is owned or leased.

figures.text: Gulf strategy: protect price rather than chase volume; rates broadly steady over nine months, occupancy fell
figures.quote: Minor said rates in the region held broadly steady over nine months, while occupancy fell around nine points. Its Gulf strategy is to protect price rather than chase volume.

figures.text: Q3: rates in the region fell for the first time this year
figures.quote: The third quarter suggests that is getting harder to hold: rates fell for the first time this year

figures.text: CEO Dillip Rajakarier: value of geographically diversified portfolio, conditions vary between markets
figures.quote: demonstrates the value of having a geographically diversified portfolio, particularly when trading conditions vary so widely between markets

figures.text: focus on protecting margins and pricing discipline, shift to fee income
figures.quote: He said the company would focus on protecting margins and pricing discipline while accelerating the shift to fee income.

figures.text: asset-light >90% of pipeline; 38 hotels signed in nine months; 2025 record 40
figures.quote: Asset-light arrangements make up more than 90% of Minor’s active development pipeline, and it signed 38 hotels in the first nine months ... its 2025 record of 40 signings.

figures.text: forward bookings Thailand and Maldives ahead of last year for Q4 and early 2027
figures.quote: Forward bookings for Thailand and the Maldives are ahead of last year for both the fourth quarter and early 2027.

figures.text: results moved by markets where Minor owns the buildings until new hotels open
figures.quote: Until those hotels open, Minor’s results will keep moving with the markets where it owns the buildings.
